properties.statement:
`propagate_change` FROM A CAPABILITY ON SHARED COMPONENTS RETURNED MOST OF THE DESIGN, AND THE ONE SIGNAL WORTH HAVING WAS BURIED IN IT. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 7.

MEASURED: seeded from a Capability allocated to a shared API and a shared client. Distance-1 was useful — the two Components plus the Requirement/Decision thread. DISTANCE-2 WAS EVERY OTHER CAPABILITY ON THOSE COMPONENTS: ~65 named, 113 truncated. His verdict: 'Edit only what the radius names is UNUSABLE. The useful signal (Interface PROVIDES/CONSUMES) was buried.'

WHY THE RADIUS BEHAVES THIS WAY AND IS NOT WRONG TO: sharing a Component is a real relation, and on a design where two Components host most of the system, one hop through them reaches most of it. The traversal is correct; what is missing is that IT REPORTS ONE KIND OF REACH. 'This Capability sits on the same Component as yours' and 'this change crosses a published Interface into something you do not own' are findings of completely different weight, arriving in one undifferentiated list.

THE INSTRUCTION THIS BREAKS is reflow2's own: step 4 of the served loop says 'Update ONLY the impacted capabilities/components/tests the blast radius names.' At 178 nodes that instruction cannot be followed, so an agent either ignores the radius or edits nothing — and both are worse than a smaller honest answer.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, and he says so: the default is a bounded SUMMARY with the full dump behind `full=true` (`chg:bl48-bl49-tool-surface`). The problem is not volume control, which exists; it is that the summary has no BANDS.

HIS PROPOSED SHAPE, held as an open question in `dec:idea-should-propagate-change-separate-crossing-an-interface-from-a-component-dump`: separate 'same Component dump' from 'crossed an Interface', and give the summary a 'sibling Capabilities on the same Component, not actually impacted' band.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether 178 is large for that design's size — he did not report the total node count, so the ratio that would make this a threshold question is unknown. This session hit the mirror image on reflow2's own graph: `propagate_change` from a TemporalFact returned ZERO impacted, because the edge connecting a defect to what it indicts is not traversed. THE SAME TOOL IS TOO WIDE ON ONE SEED TYPE AND SILENT ON ANOTHER.
